Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_SolarModule: A 160 W solar module. Mount it flat, on a wall or on a ground rack.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_HomemadeSolarMod: Salvaged cells under glass. Rated 160 W, but it never makes more than 96 W.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_SolarCells: Cells salvaged from solar gadgets. Sixteen make a homemade solar module.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_SolarFlat: One module lying flat, on a roof or the ground. Best in summer; snow settles on it.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_SolarWall: One module on an outside wall, facing south or east. Best in winter; snow slides off, and storms can't reach it.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_SolarRackWood: Two modules tilted toward the sun. Sheds snow within a couple of hours, but storms rattle a wooden rack.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_SolarRackMetal: Two modules tilted toward the sun. Sheds snow within a couple of hours and stands up to storms.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_BatteryBox: Holds 2 batteries, an inverter and a car battery charger. Takes 2 inputs, with no room for a charge controller. Goes indoors.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_BatteryRackWood: Holds 6 batteries, an inverter, 2 chargers and 2 charge controllers. Goes indoors.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_BatteryRackMetal: Holds 8 batteries, an inverter, 2 chargers and 2 charge controllers. Goes indoors.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_BatteryBankWood: Holds 12 batteries, 2 inverters, 2 chargers and 4 charge controllers. Goes indoors.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_BatteryBankMetal: Holds 16 batteries, 2 inverters, 2 chargers and 4 charge controllers. Goes indoors.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_PlugInInverter: Turns a battery bank's stored power into household current for everything around it, as a generator would. Carries up to 300 W at once; switch on more and the power cuts out.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_PowerInverter: Turns a battery bank's stored power into household current for everything around it, as a generator would. Carries up to 600 W at once; switch on more and the power cuts out.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_InverterCharger: The biggest inverter: carries up to 1000 W at once from a battery bank. Its built-in charger also fills the batteries, ten times as fast as a car battery charger, whenever the grid or a running generator reaches the bank.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_MakeshiftInverte: A transformer run backwards on a heatsink of transistors. Carries up to 300 W from a battery bank, like a plug-in inverter, but wastes a quarter of what passes through it, idles hotter and wears out sooner.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_HomemadeInverter: A rewound microwave transformer with two heatsinks of transistors. Carries up to 600 W from a battery bank, like a power inverter, but wastes a fifth of what passes through it, idles hotter and wears out sooner.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_MicrowaveTransfo: Salvaged from a microwave oven. Rewound, it is the heart of a homemade inverter.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_ChargeController: Regulates the charge coming in from panels, wind chargers and treadmills. A battery bank takes 2 inputs on its own; each controller wired in adds 7. A panel, scoop rotor or treadmill uses 1, a bladed wind charger 3.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_SolarFailsafe: Place it under a backup generator. It starts the generator when the battery bank runs low.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_DeepCycleBattery: Built to be run down and recharged. Goes in a battery bank, or in a vehicle, where it runs the lights and radio twice as long as a car battery.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_L16Battery: A heavy 6 V battery for battery banks. Too low a voltage for a vehicle.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_JarBattery: Six glass-jar cells in a sand tray, wired as one 12 V battery. Heavy for what it holds and soon worn out. Battery banks only: open jars would spill in a vehicle.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_BatteryCase: A stripped battery's case. New plates and acid rebuild it.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_WornBatteryPlate: Sulfated lead plates. Recast them at a furnace: a third of the lead skims off as dross, so three worn sets cast two.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_BatteryPlates: Fresh lead plates for rebuilding a battery or making a jar battery.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_BatteryPlateMold: Fired clay. Lead battery plates are cast in it.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_BatteryElectroly: A litre of battery acid, for rebuilding a battery.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_SolarMaintainer: Clip it to a vehicle to keep its battery charged in daylight.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_SolarCellCharger: Place it outdoors and load it with up to 4 batteries. Charges them in daylight.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_SolarGardenLight: Place it on the ground outdoors. It charges by day and glows at night, in the colour of its light bulb.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_UnmountGivesModu: Gives back the modules, each in the condition it went in.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_TakeApartGivesBu: Gives back the light bulb too, if it has one.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_RepairCrackedMod: Adds 20 condition to a cracked module, up to 55 (40 for a homemade one), less 10 for each time it was sealed. The glass stays cracked.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_ReglazeModule: New glass brings a module with only light cracks back to new. Heavy cracks, or cracks bad enough to need sealing, reached the cells too: it comes back to 90%% of new. Its old seals no longer count.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_ModuleSealedFull: Sealed as far as sealing goes. Unmount the module and reglaze it.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_PanelSealedFully: Sealed as far as sealing goes. Take the panel off in the mechanics window and reglaze its module.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_TakeApartShatter: Only a shattered module, at no condition, comes apart for its cells.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_ServiceBattery: Adds 10 condition, up to the battery's repair limit: 85, less 10 for each time it was repaired. Its charge stays.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_ReconditionBatte: Brings the battery to its repair limit (85, less 10 for each time it was repaired) and leaves it empty. Wood ash does what baking soda does.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_RecastBatteryPla: A third of the lead skims off as dross, so three worn sets cast two. A lead pipe can stand in for the third, and charcoal turns the dross back into plates.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_ReduceLeadDross: Charcoal takes the oxygen back out of the dross: one set of plates from each skimming, so recast lead is never lost.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_CastBatteryPlate: Three lead pipes cast one set of plates, with no battery case needed: enough for a jar battery.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_RebuildCarBatter: Gives back the car battery the case came from, as new and empty.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_MakeJarBattery: Any empty glass jars, or glazed clay jars. The battery comes out as new, and empty.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_GardenLightOutdo: Garden lights go on the ground outdoors.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_BankIndoorsOnly: Battery banks go indoors, inside a building.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_NotAPart: Only batteries, inverters, car battery chargers and charge controllers can be wired in.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_NothingToWire: Carry a battery, an inverter, a car battery charger or a charge controller to wire it in.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_NoSlot: The bank has no room for another one of these.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_TooDark: It's too dark to see what you're doing.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_NeedSnowTool: Needs a broom or a snow shovel.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_NeedsFittingBlad: Needs blades this wind charger takes.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_NoInputSlot: The bank has no free input for it. Charge controllers add more, in a battery rack or bank.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_BankNotConnected: The battery bank isn't connected yet. Connect Bank from its own menu first.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_NoInverter: The bank has no working inverter.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_NoBatteries: The bank has no working batteries.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_BarrelDigester: A drum of rotting scraps and manure that makes gas once it gets going, into garbage bags. Small, stinks the most, and stops in the cold.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_InsulatedDigeste: A drum boxed in straw and planks under a floating gas drum. Bigger, works into the fall, smells less.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_BrickDome: A dome of bricks or stone blocks over a pit dug in the ground, so it's built only on earth, grass or sand. Keeps itself warm on its own gas and works all winter. Hard to build; it hardly smells.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_WoodAsh: Wood ash. Compostable, and an alkali that settles a sour digester or cleans a battery for servicing in place of baking soda.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_LeadDross: Lead burnt to oxide, skimmed off a recast. Reduce it with charcoal at a furnace for a set of plates.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_NoSludge: Not enough sludge to fill a bag.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_NeedsSack: Needs an empty sack or a compost bag with room in it.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_NoGasBags: Only a barrel digester takes gas bags.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_NoGasBag: There's no gas bag on it.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_NotBarrel: Only a barrel digester can be upgraded.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_TarpGasBag: A gas bag sewn from a tarp for a barrel digester. Holds more than garbage bags and lasts far longer.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_IronSponge: Splinters and filed iron scrap, damped and left to rust together. Packs a scrubber the way steel wool does, and airs out to work again.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_SpentIronSponge: Black with what it took out of the gas. Damped and aired out, it rusts back into an Iron Sponge, a little less each time.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_TakeSludge: Spent sludge comes out as compost. The tank slows once it's nearly full.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_VentGas: Lets the gas out, so a gas bag can come off. Careful indoors: it fills the building with fumes for a while.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_FitGarbageBags: Cheap and quick, but they tear before long.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_FitTarpGasBag: Holds more gas than garbage bags and lasts far longer.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_TakeOffGasBag: A tarp gas bag comes off whole, to mend or fit elsewhere. Garbage bags are done for.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_Upgrade: Keeps it from getting too cold and holds more feed. The barrel goes in a box of planks and straw, with a second drum floating on top to hold the gas.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_FillByPump: Slow, tiring work that only fills it partway.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_FillByCompressor: Fills it all the way where there's power, once the gas is scrubbed.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_FitScrubber: Cleans the gas so a compressor can fill a tank all the way. Keep its water and packing refilled.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_RefillScrubberWa: Plain water cleans the gas for a while.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_RefillScrubberAs: Wood ash in the water makes it last longer.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_RefillScrubberLi: Quicklime in the water makes it last longest.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_RefillScrubberWo: Steel wool catches what the water misses. Pack in fresh once it's spent.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_RefillScrubberSp: Packs it in place of steel wool. The spent sponge comes back out at the next packing, to air out.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_GasConversionKit: A mixer valve, hose and clamps that let a generator run on gas from a digester or a gasifier. On clean gas it carries a house and a charging battery bank; on a gasifier's dirtier gas, less.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_HasKit: This generator already has a Gas Conversion Kit.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_NoKit: This generator has no Gas Conversion Kit.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_HasLine: A gas line is already connected.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_DigesterOutOfRea: The digester is too far away, or on another floor.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_NoDigesterInReac: No digester within %1 squares on this floor, and no gasifier beside the generator.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_RemoveKitFirst: Remove the Gas Conversion Kit first.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_NeedsVessel: Needs a propane tank, a welding torch or a propane lantern bottle.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_NoPower: Needs power here to run the compressor.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_PumpLimit: A tire pump can't push it any fuller.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_NeedsScrubbed: Past what a tire pump can push, the compressor needs scrubbed gas: refill the scrubber.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_FridgeCompressor: Salvaged from a fridge. Plugged in where there is power, it presses scrubbed biogas into a propane tank.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_GasHeater: Burns a little biogas from a digester beside it to keep the digester warm, or a cold room.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_NoDigesterNear: There's no digester with gas beside it.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_PrimitiveGasifie: Burns wood to make gas for a generator beside it with a Gas Conversion Kit. Small, tarry and needs cleaning often.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_Gasifier: Burns wood to make gas for a generator beside it with a Gas Conversion Kit. A full hopper runs it nearly as long as a tank of gasoline.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_AdvancedGasifier: Burns wood or, best, charcoal to make gas for a generator beside it with a Gas Conversion Kit. Little tar and little cleaning.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_TarryPacking: A gasifier filter's packing, soaked with tar. Burns in the gasifier's hopper.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_NoWood: There's no wood in the hopper.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_LittleAsh: There's too little ash to clean out.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_GasifierNotBesid: A gasifier must stand right beside the generator.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_WontTakeCondensa: That won't take it. Drained hot, it needs metal, glass or a pot.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_TreadmillMotor: A treadmill's motor. Turn it and it makes power: the generator of the scoop rotor and the treadmill wind charger.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_ScoopRotor: Two half-drum scoops turning a treadmill motor on a short pole. Weak and slow, but it takes any wind and never needs the brake. Connect it to a bank like a panel.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_TreadmillNotConn: Connect it to a bank first, or the running goes nowhere.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_TreadmillNoPower: There's no power for its motor. Wire the motor and connect it to a battery bank, and running on it makes power instead.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_TreadmillWindCha: Three blades on a treadmill motor, high on a pipe mast. Real power in a good wind; in a gale it strains, and left unbraked its blades may break. Uses three inputs, so the bank needs a charge controller.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_CarAlternatorWin: Three blades on a pipe mast, belted up to a car's alternator. More power than a treadmill motor in any wind; in a gale it strains, and left unbraked its blades may break. Uses three inputs, so the bank needs a charge controller.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_WindTurbine: Three blades on a homemade alternator, on a braced two-storey mast. The best of them: in a gale its tail swings it aside and it keeps most of its power, and its blades hold through a fiercer gale than on the other chargers. Uses three inputs, so the bank needs a charge controller.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_Blades: Blades for a treadmill or car alternator wind charger or a homebuilt wind turbine; a spare set mends any of them a storm broke, whatever blades it had. Pipe blades snap in a lesser gale than carved wood.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_SteelBlades: Blades for a treadmill or car alternator wind charger or a homebuilt wind turbine; a spare set mends any of them a storm broke. They hold in a fiercer gale than wood or pipe. A furnace melts them down.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_BrokenWoodenBlad: What a storm left of a set of carved blades. Good for a fire.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_BrokenPipeBlades: What a storm left of a set of plastic pipe blades. No good for anything now.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_BrokenSteelBlade: What a storm left of a set of forged steel blades. A blast furnace melts the steel back out of them.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_HomemadeAlternat: Speaker magnets on a car's brake hub, turning past hand-wound coils: the generator of the homebuilt wind turbine, the best wind charger.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_CarAlternator: A car's alternator, taken out of a car or cut from a smashed wreck. Belted to a set of blades, it turns a car alternator wind charger.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_NotACar: Only an intact car's engine has an alternator to work on.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_AlternatorGone: This car's alternator has already been taken out.
Tooltip_RenewableEnergy_AlternatorFitted: This car still has its alternator.
